messages:
Grace: Hey team, hitting 403s when calling /v1/generate with a key that used to work. Started after we upgraded our plan yesterday. Body says something about "invalid_api_key" but I'm sure the key is fine. Can someone check?

Alex: Sorry you're blocked, Grace. Can you paste a minimal repro request (no secrets) and the exact response body? Also which org/account id?

Grace: Org 92834. Repro (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwdx-large", "input":"test"}'
```
Response: 403 Forbidden, body: `{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\", \"message\":\"Invalid credentials\"}`

Grace: We rolled from Free -> Startup plan and the console shows model access. Billing shows active.

Alex: Thanks. Priya, tagging eng for entitlement checks - looks like support-side mapping might be collapsing entitlement failures into auth errors. Any quick logs you can pull for org 92834?

entitlement-bot: entitlement-check (org:92834) => result: MISSING_ENTITLEMENT for feature:rwdx-large_generation (evaluated at 2024-09-03T16:02:12Z).

Priya: I pulled the request trace. The entitlement service returned MISSING_ENTITLEMENT, but our auth middleware has a catch-all that maps non-200 from entitlement-service -> 401/403 with code `invalid_api_key`. That's bad UX.

Priya: Root cause: when plan assignment happened there was a short race where new plan mappings weren't propagated to the entitlement cache on our edge. Entitlement service returned explicit missing entitlement, but middleware translated to `invalid_api_key`.

Sam: From billing: payment and plan upgrade completed successfully (txn id tx_2391). No invoice holds. So this is not a payment-blocking 403.

Alex: Grace — for a quick workaround, can you create a new API key in the console and try again? That should hit the fresh user cache and bypass the stale edge entry.

Grace: Ok making a new key now... yep new key works, generates fine. So that confirms stale cache. Thanks.

Priya: Next steps from eng: 1) fix middleware mapping so entitlement failures surface as clear error code `ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED` and message "model not enabled for your plan" (won't say invalid_api_key), 2) add a cache invalidation hook on plan-change events, 3) add metrics/alert when entitlement-service responses cause >1% auth-mapped failures.

Alex: Support action item: update KB entry to include this troubleshooting step (create new key to bypass edge cache) and document how to differentiate true auth failures (401) vs plan gating (403+ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED).

Priya: Quick patch landed to change mapping (will be in next deploy, ETA 30m). I'll also drop a temporary header X-Entitlement-Status on failures so support can triage until the message change rolls out. Example failure body that will be emitted after patch: `{\"error\":\"forbidden\", \"code\":\"ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED\", \"message\":\"Model rwdx-large not enabled for your plan\"}`

Sam: Noted for billing: we'll add a small UI flag on the plan page to show which models/features are included per tier to reduce confusion.

Alex: Grace — closing loop: we verified cause (cache / mapping), workaround (new API key), and mitigations (patch + KB + UI change). Any objections to closing this? :white_check_mark:

Grace: No objections, thanks all. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :pray:

Priya: Will monitor rollout and post here when mapping change is live.

entitlement-bot: deploy: entitlement-mapping-fix -> success (deploy id dpl-7711)

Priya: Mapping change is live and logs show 92834 requests now returning ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED when appropriate. Pushing KB update to /docs/support/entitlement-gating.md.

Alex: Marking resolved. If Grace sees anything else ping me and we'll reopen.

Grace: All good. Thanks again!
